# New renderings, iliad-128 (20.103–198)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπεν ἄναξ Διὸς υἱὸς Ἀπόλλων (20.103, whole-line reply introduction) | "Him then in turn addressed the lord, the son of Zeus, Apollo:" | "Then lord Apollo, the son of Zeus, spoke to him in turn:" | masculine of the table’s τὴν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπεν … (7.37); "answered" (kept for ἀμείβομαι) |
| τὴν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα Ποσειδάων ἐνοσίχθων (20.132, whole-line reply formula) | "Her then answered Poseidon earth-shaker:" | "Then Poseidon earth-shaker answered her:" | follows the table’s τὴν/τὸν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα … (1.551) with ἐνοσίχθων "earth-shaker" (7.445) |
| ἣ δ’ ἄμυδις στήσασα θεοὺς μετὰ μῦθον ἔειπε (20.114, whole line) | "And she, having made the gods stand together, among them spoke a speech:" | "She gathered the gods together and spoke among them:" | "called an assembly" (ἀγορή), "addressed" (reserved for προσέειπε); μετὰ μῦθον ἔειπε as in the table’s 3.303 row |
| ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας ἡγήσατο κυανοχαίτης (20.144) | "So then, having spoken, led the way the dark-haired one" | "So he spoke, and the dark-haired one led the way" | "Poseidon" (the Greek withholds the name); "dark-maned"; κυανοχαίτης "dark-haired" as the table’s κυανοχαῖτα Ποσειδάων |
| ὣς οἳ μέν ῥ’ ἑκάτερθε καθήατο μητιόωντες βουλάς (20.153) | "So they, on either side, were sitting, planning counsels;" | "So they sat on either side, making their plans;" | "plotting", "devising"; μητιάω "plan", βουλή "counsel" in `l`, "plans" in `i` |
| τὸν πρότερος προσέειπε ποδάρκης δῖος Ἀχιλλεύς (20.177, whole-line speech introduction) | "him first addressed swift-footed, heavenly Achilles:" | "swift-footed, heavenly Achilles spoke to him first:" | "fleet-footed" (ποδώκης), "swift of foot" (πόδας ὠκύς); the table’s ποδάρκης row (1.121) and τὴν πρότερος προσέειπεν … (7.23) |
| Ἄρηα πτολίπορθον (20.152) | "Ares the city-sacking" | "Ares, the city-sacker" | follows the table’s Ἀχιλλῆα πτολίπορθον (8.372) |
| ἔξοχ’ ἄριστοι (δύο δ’ ἀνέρες ἔξοχ’ ἄριστοι, 20.158) | "far the best" | "far the best" | "above all others the best" (the first draft), "outstanding", "pre-eminent"; follows the shipped Odyssey 4.629 (odyssey-019) ἔξοχ’ ἄριστοι "far the best" |
| ἀμφίχυτον (τεῖχος … ἀμφίχυτον, 20.145; ἀμφί + χέω "pour") | "heaped-around" | "heaped up around" | "round-built", "encircling", "mounded"; keeps the pouring/heaping of χέω and does not say what material |
| κῆτος (20.147) | "sea-monster" | "sea-monster" | "whale", "sea-beast"; the table’s κῆτος "sea-monster" (13.27) |
| δυσηλεγής (πολέμοιο, 20.154; sense uncertain) | "painful" | "painful" (+ note: sense not certain) | "grievous" (reserved for ἀλεγεινός), "pitiless" (a second guess); follows the Odyssey table (22.325) |
| κάρκαιρε (20.157; rare verb, meaning not known) | "shook" | "shook" (+ note: meaning not known, "shook" a guess from the picture) | "rang", "resounded", "trembled" (each picks another guess) |
| ἀντιόωντες (+ genitive μάχης, 20.125) | "meeting" | "to meet" | "to join", "to take part in" (each decides more than the verb says); follows the table’s ἀντιάω "meet" (6.127) |
| ἤϊε Φοῖβε (20.152) | "Ēïe Phoebus" | "Phoebus" (+ note: ἤϊε left out, meaning not known) | "healer", "Paean"; follows the table (15.365) |
| νεῖκος … φυλόπιδος (20.140–141) | "a quarrel … of the din of battle" | "a quarrel of the din of battle" | "strife" (ἔρις), "battle-cry"; νεῖκος "quarrel", φύλοπις "the din of battle" |
| παρ’ ἐκ νόον (μὴ χαλέπαινε παρ’ ἐκ νόον, 20.133) | "beyond sense" | "beyond reason" | "against your will", "out of your mind" (each moves the phrase); the note gives παρέκ + νόον "mind" |
| ἀνεμώλιοι (20.123, of the gods who protect the Trojans) | "empty" | "empty" | "windy", "vain", "useless"; follows the table’s ἀνεμώλιος "empty" (4.355) |
| τιμῆς τῆς Πριάμου (20.181) | "the honour of Priam" | "the honour that Priam holds" (+ note: his standing as king) | "throne", "kingdom", "rank" (each names the thing the Greek leaves as "honour") |
| ἀτίζων (20.166; rare verb) | "making light of" | "paying them no heed" | "scorning", "despising" (each decides the feeling); ἀτίζω "slight" |
| γλαυκιόων (20.172; rare verb, from γλαυκός "gleaming") | "glaring" | "glaring" | "with glittering eyes", "flashing" (supply "eyes", which the Greek does not name) |
| μένει (of the lion, 20.172) | "in fury" | "in his fury" | "might" (the table keeps it for μένος of a fighter, 20.110 and 20.174), "courage"; the table’s μένος of anger, "fury" |
| κραδίῃ … ἦτορ (20.169) | "in his heart groans the valiant heart" | "in his heart the valiant heart groans" | "breast" for κραδίη, "spirit" (kept for θυμός); both words are "heart", with ἄλκιμον ἦτορ "valiant heart" (5.529) |
| μεθορμηθείς (20.192; "set out", the μετά not clear) | "having set out in pursuit" | "I set out in pursuit" (+ note: after whom the Greek does not say) | "having followed you", "having rushed upon it" (each supplies an object) |
| μετατροπαλίζεο (20.190) | "keep turning round" | "keep turning round" | "look back" (a picture the verb does not give), "turned back and forth" |
| ἐρύεσθαι (οὐ νῦν ἐρύεσθαι ὀΐομαι, 20.195) | "to rescue" | "you will be rescued" (+ note: who rescues and whom is left out) | "the gods will rescue you" (supplies a subject); ἐρύομαι "rescue", the same verb as ἐρρύσατο "rescued" in 20.194 |
| ἐξεναρίξῃς (20.181) | "despoil" | "kill me and strip me of my armour" | "slay"; follows the table’s ἐξεναρίζω "killed and stripped of his armour" (4.488) |
| ληϊάδας γυναῖκας (20.193) | "the women taken as spoil" | "the women taken as spoil" | "captive women" (loses ληΐς "booty"), "plundered women" |
| νέμηαι (20.185) | "that you may occupy it" | "for you to occupy" | follows the published iliad-037 (6.194–195, ὄφρα νέμοιτο "that he might occupy it") |

Reuse and departures: 20.110 and 20.111 follow the published English of iliad-093 and iliad-026 (20.110 ends in a comma here, not a full stop, so `i` ends with a comma too; in 20.111 the "he" is Aeneas, as the note says); 20.159, 20.176 and 20.196–198 follow iliad-037, iliad-016 and iliad-108 (the closing lines differ from iliad-108 only by a comma in the Greek). No departure from an Odyssey rendering. At review, ἐναργεῖς (20.131) and ἀεσίφρων (20.183) were brought back to the existing table rows (Odyssey 7.201 "manifest" / "in manifest form"; Odyssey 21.302 "senseless") and their rows here removed; ἔξοχ’ ἄριστοι follows Odyssey 4.629.
